Subject: Data retention & deletion SLAs — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Sanjeev / Amaya security team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to understand your regulatory constraints and the questions your security team raised. Quick recap and proposed next steps specifically on data retention / deletion and backups, per your ask: 

Summary of asks from call:
- Clarify deletion SLAs for user-requested deletions (primary storage vs backups)
- Log retention policy (access logs, audit logs, application logs)
- SOC 2 status and expected timeline for Type II report
- Kick off vendor security questionnaire

Our proposed answers / next steps: 
1) Deletion SLAs (primary data): We can commit to removing user-requested data from active primary storage within 30 days of the request. Deletion includes model inputs/outputs stored as part of the session and associated metadata.

2) Backups & snapshots: Backups are maintained for disaster recovery. We keep snapshot backups for up to 90 days by default. We apply a logical-delete flag to records immediately upon a deletion request; physical removal from backup snapshots follows the standard retention lifecycle (we can discuss a shorter backup retention window in Private deployments).

3) Logs: Default retention for security/audit logs is 365 days to support incident investigations. Application-level logs can be configured per-customer; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can change retention to meet GDPR/HIPAA requirements.

4) SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 in progress; we have a SOC 2 Type II audit planned and expect Type II evidence to be available in Q3 2026. In the meantime, I attached a one-page SOC 2 summary and our controls roadmap.

5) Vendor questionnaire: Happy to kick this off. If you share the questionnaire, I’ll route to our security team (cc'ed: neha and rishi) and we’ll aim to return an initial pass within 5 business days.

Action items I propose:
- Sanjeev: send the vendor security questionnaire (or a link) and a prioritized list of retention obligations you need (e.g., specific retention windows for PHI, audit logs to be shorter).
- Redwood (me): share our data retention doc + SOC2 summary (attached).
- Redwood security (neha/rishi): will review questionnaire and follow up on any technical clarifications.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-overview.pdf (summary), soc2-summary.pdf (controls snapshot)

If that sounds right I’ll wait for the questionnaire and we’ll schedule a follow-up if any items need a deeper technical call.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our side before we send over the questionnaire: 

1) Backups: when you say "logical-delete flag" is applied immediately, can you confirm whether data referenced in a snapshots object will remain recoverable by your internal DR process for the full 90 days? In other words, do you have a process to ensure customer-initiated deletions are not restorable from snapshots beyond X days?

2) If Amaya is subject to a deletion request under GDPR (data subject request) or a customer requests deletion of PHI under HIPAA, what is the commitment around the backup window? We need to understand whether we should expect a maximum of 30 days for full non-recoverability or longer.

3) Logs: we need separation between audit logs (who accessed what) and application/request logs (model inputs/outputs). Audit logs are business-critical and should be retained for at least 12 months, but we need to know how they’re scoped and whether they contain any model input data.

4) SOC 2: can you share the most recent control gaps and the expected date for Type II availability? Also want to know whether encryption at rest uses customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) as an option.

We’ll attach the questionnaire (vendor_security_v1.pdf) in a follow-up email. In parallel we’ll prepare a short list of retention obligations for Amaya (PHI-specific windows).

—Sanjeev

Hi Sanjeev — quick answers inline below, happy to get more granular once we see the questionnaire.

1) Backups / snapshots: Correct — snapshots are kept for up to 90 days for DR. When a deletion request is received we mark the record as deleted immediately in primary storage. For snapshots, we do not automatically restore deleted data for business-as-usual DR restores once the deletion flag is present; however, because snapshots are immutable objects, the data technically remains in snapshot artifacts until the retention lifecycle removes them. Practically, we can offer a shorter backup retention window under Dedicated/Private deployments or provide a contractual acceptance that logical deletes are applied immediately and the recovery-from-snapshot window is limited to 30 days for Amaya (we can add that as an SLA clause).

2) GDPR/HIPAA deletions: Standard offering: primary deletion within 30 days; backups subject to the retention lifecycle up to 90 days. For customers with strict regulatory requirements (like HIPAA-covered entities), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where we can configure backup retention to 30 days and support customer-managed keys. We can include a clause in the DPA addressing backup lifecycles and explicit commitments for PHI.

3) Logs: Audit logs (who/when) do not contain full model input content. Application/request logs used for troubleshooting may contain redacted inputs; we redact sensitive fields by default and can apply stricter redaction for PHI. Default audit log retention: 365 days. If you need shorter or longer retention we can discuss.

4) SOC 2 and encryption: We are currently completing SOC 2 Type II; expected evidence delivery Q3 2026. We support encryption at rest with provider-managed KMS by default; customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. I’ve attached the SOC2 summary with controls and expected milestones.

Next steps: Please send the questionnaire and your prioritized retention windows. If Amaya wants contractual changes (e.g., backup retention <=30 days, CMK), we can escalate and surface those in the DPA/technical addendum.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sanjeev / team,

Following up from Marissa's answers with a bit more technical detail from our security operations side: 

- Backups implementation: We take incremental snapshots stored in encrypted S3 buckets with lifecycle policies. Snapshots are immutable; retention is controlled by lifecycle rules (default 90 days). When a deletion request occurs, we flag the record and remove it from primary stores within 30 days. For additional assurance, we can implement an expedited snapshot purge process for Dedicated/Private customers where snapshots matching a deletion predicate are removed within a 30-day window.

- Restore policy: Day-0 restores from snapshots are possible up to the retention period; however, our DR runbooks will not restore records flagged as deleted without an explicit business reason. We can add an audit trail entry and attestation if you require non-recoverability evidence.

- Access & audit logs: Stored separately from application data, encrypted, and immutably indexed for forensic use. By default retention is 365 days; exportable on request. Audit logs do not contain model input payloads.

- Next step for the questionnaire: I’ve attached a short kickoff doc (vendor-questionnaire-kickoff.docx) indicating who on our side will own which sections (security controls: neha_kapoor; infra: rishi_malhotra; legal/compliance: marissa_cole). If you want to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for the questionnaire we can do that later this week.

Thanks,
